_about: Legendary and Mythical Pokémon guide. Hand-written from the event scripts the v105 ROM was built from; tools/legendaries.py checks every entry against the ROM (species flags, script symbols, levels) and against data/availability.json, and refuses to pass if an obtainable Legendary or Mythical Pokémon has no complete entry. Markup: [[region/slug|text]] chapter link, {{item:Name}}, {{map:MapKey|text}}, {{mon:SPECIES_X|text}}, {{quest:id|text}}, ||story spoiler||. `rom` rows are [symbol, species constant, level] and are verified byte-for-byte.
intro: Every Legendary and Mythical Pokémon you can actually catch in Project Blonde, with the place, the conditions and the steps. Thirty-two can be obtained. Nothing here is copied from the official games: each entry is read from this game’s own event scripts and checked against the release build.
Most of these are single visible Pokémon that you walk up to. Save before you talk to one.
rules: For almost every fixed encounter, fleeing leaves the Pokémon where it is, or it is back when you re-enter the area. The one exception is Celebi’s shrine battle.
A knock-out is not the end
A Pokémon you defeat leaves, but most return when you next enter the Hall of Fame as Kanto Champion. See {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.
Nothing here is missed for good
No entry on this page can be lost permanently. The worst case is a wait until your next League win.

quests.title: How legendaries return
p: Your first Hall of Fame entry, after the Johto League, does not reset anything. Every later one does. Once you hold sixteen Badges and re-enter the Indigo Plateau as described in [[kanto/kanto-league|The Kanto League]], each Hall of Fame entry there puts the following back, whether you caught them before or not:

Back at their posts: Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, Mewtwo, Ho-Oh and Lugia (both at Level 70), the Latias or Latios on Southern Island, Mew, Deoxys, the six Regis of Sinjoh including Regigigas, and the Mt. Moon rock that calls Jirachi.
Released again: Raikou and Entei in Johto and your chosen Latias or Latios in Kanto. A roamer that was still at large is replaced by a fresh one.

Only if you got far enough: Suicune returns to Route 25 once you have fought it there. A second Celebi appears in Ilex Forest once you have caught the first; if you did not catch it, the GS Ball reappears in the Ruins of Alph instead. The four Tapu return once Samson Oak has given you the Beast Ball. Arceus returns once Steven has congratulated you in its hall.

The same League win is also what makes you Kanto Champion the first time. That title is the key to three things on this page: the guard leaves Cerulean Cave, Steven hands over the {{item:Eon Ticket}} and a woman in Olivine City hands over the {{item:Aurora Ticket}}.
Kyogre, Groudon and Rayquaza follow Hoenn’s rule, not this one: see their entries.

quests.title: The seventeen plates of Sinjoh
quests.sub: The quest behind six Regis and Arceus
marker: Item ball. This starts the Sinjoh story.
need: Access to Mt. Silver: sixteen Badges, Surf and Waterfall. See [[kanto/mt-silver|Mt. Silver]].
A team for Level 80 single Pokémon with fixed movesets, and for Steven.
steps: Pick up the {{item:Azure Flute}}, an item ball on {{map:MtSilver_2F_hns|Mt. Silver 2F}}.

Go to the Pokémon Center outside Mt. Silver and talk to the researcher from the Pewter museum. She notices the flute, a window explains that this is extra content, and she asks whether you are ready. Say Yes. She takes you to a branch of the cave on 1F, where a scientist speaks to you and leaves. From now on she will take you there again whenever you ask.

Follow the branch into {{map:SnowsweptCavern_hns|Snowswept Cavern}}. A Machamp stands by a boulder. Talk to it and accept: it fights at Level 75 and cannot be caught. When it goes down it drops the {{item:Fist Plate}} and the boulder is cleared. This is plate 1.
Carry on to {{map:Route49_hns|Route 49}}, where a Kimono Girl meets you, then into the Kimono Girls’ hideout in {{map:NewSinjoh_hns|New Sinjoh}}.

Go on to the research lab at the {{map:SinjohRuins_hns|Sinjoh Ruins}}. Steven is there with a team from Devon. He explains that seventeen plates matter to the ruins and asks for your help. He keeps asking until you say Yes.

Seven Trainers now agree to battle, and each gives a plate when beaten: Skylar on Route 49 ({{item:Sky Plate}}); Miharu, Youko and Shizuko in the Kimono hideout ({{item:Meadow Plate}}, {{item:Icicle Plate}}, {{item:Pixie Plate}}); Mualani in the {{map:NewSinjoh_HotSprings_hns|hot springs}} ({{item:Splash Plate}}); Wessel and Finley on {{map:Route50_hns|Route 50}} ({{item:Iron Plate}}, {{item:Draco Plate}}). Before you have agreed to help Steven they only talk.

Eight Noble Pokémon guard the rest. At each Noble’s spot the game says “The Azure Flute is reacting. Play the flute?” Say Yes and the Noble appears; talk to it to fight. All are Level 80, cannot be caught, and drop a plate: Overqwil ({{item:Dread Plate}}) and Wyrdeer ({{item:Mind Plate}}) on Route 49; Sneasler ({{item:Toxic Plate}}) in Snowswept Cavern; Hisuian Arcanine ({{item:Flame Plate}}) and Ursaluna ({{item:Earth Plate}}) in the hot springs; Kleavor ({{item:Insect Plate}}) and Hisuian Electrode ({{item:Zap Plate}}) on Route 50; Hisuian Typhlosion ({{item:Spooky Plate}}) in the old house in New Sinjoh.

Steven phones as the count rises. At 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 plates a chamber under the ruins opens: Regirock, Regice, Registeel, Regieleki and Regidrago, in that order. You can go and catch each as it opens.
At 16 plates Steven calls you back. Enter the lab for a scene with the plates, after which you are taken outside to the ruins and a stairway opens.

Steven waits on the landing. Answer Yes when he asks if you are ready and beat him. He gives you the {{item:Stone Plate}}, the seventeenth, and heals your party. The hall above is now open: continue with {{mon:SPECIES_ARCEUS_NORMAL|Arceus}}.
after: The plates are held items and are yours to keep.
The exact spot of each Noble was not walked for this guide. The flute prompt appears when you step on the right tiles; the area maps are linked above.

marker: Where it waits on later visits.
Step here in the story and the dance begins.
entries.start: On Route 39, near Moomoo Farm, a shadow passes overhead and Baoba asks what colour it was. Your answer picks your story legend. Gold is Ho-Oh.
need: If you answered Gold: all eight Johto Badges, the {{item:Rainbow Wing}} and the {{item:Clear Bell}}.
If you answered Silver: reach Pewter City in Kanto. The story gave you Lugia; Ho-Oh comes second.
steps: Gold. Clear the Goldenrod Radio Tower. The Director gives you the Rainbow Wing: see [[johto/radio-tower|Goldenrod Radio Tower]].
With eight Badges, beat the Kimono Girls in Ecruteak’s theater. They give you the Clear Bell and go ahead to the tower: see [[johto/kimono-girls|The Kimono Girls]].
Go north through the gatehouse. The sage steps aside when he hears the bell. Cross Bellchime Trail and climb Tin Tower to the roof.
Walk forward. The Kimono Girls dance and Ho-Oh descends. Talk to it from below.
Silver. In Pewter City, talk to the old man. He gives you the Rainbow Wing he found in Johto. The Tin Tower’s sage now lets you through without a bell, and Ho-Oh is already on the roof at Level 70.
encounter: A single wild battle. It can be caught.
Level 50 when it is your story legend, Level 70 from the Pewter old man’s wing and on every later return.
after: If you catch or defeat it, it leaves and the Kimono Girls return to the theater.
Ho-Oh is back on the roof at Level 70 after each later League win: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, at Level 70 after each later League win
facts.If you flee: It stays. Talk to it again.
facts.If you defeat it: It flies away until your next League win

If you answered Gold: reach Pewter City in Kanto. The story gave you Ho-Oh; Lugia comes second.
steps: Silver. Clear the Goldenrod Radio Tower. The Director gives you the Silver Wing instead of the Rainbow Wing.
Beat the Kimono Girls in Ecruteak’s theater. They give you the Tidal Bell and leave for the Whirl Islands.
Surf to the Whirl Islands on Route 41 and work down to the Lugia chamber. The Tentacruel that blocked the way leave once the Kimono Girls have given you the bell.
Walk up to the Kimono Girls in the chamber. They dance, fog rolls in and Lugia rises. Talk to it.
Gold. In Pewter City, talk to the old man. He gives you the Silver Wing he found in Johto, the Tentacruel leaves, and Lugia is already in the chamber at Level 70.
encounter: A single wild battle. It can be caught.
Level 50 when it is your story legend, Level 70 from the Pewter old man’s wing and on every later return.

Lugia is back in the chamber at Level 70 after each later League win: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.If you flee: It stays. Talk to it again.

marker: They run when you come close.
entries.start: The basement of the Burned Tower in Ecruteak City.
need: Reach Ecruteak City. No Badge is checked.
steps: Enter the Burned Tower and drop to the basement. Walk up to the three beasts: they wake and scatter. See [[johto/ecruteak-city|Ecruteak City]].
From that moment Raikou is somewhere on Johto’s routes: Routes 29 to 39, 42 to 46 and 48. It is never in a town or a cave, and Routes 40, 41 and 47 are not on its path.
Walk in the grass or Surf on those routes. When Raikou is on the route you are on, each wild encounter has a one-in-four chance of being Raikou instead.
It changes route as you travel, and moves somewhere new after every battle.
encounter: A wild battle with its own music. It can be caught.
Its HP and status are kept between meetings, so damage adds up.
A Repel keeps it away if your leading Pokémon is above Level 40.
after: Raikou is released again after each later League win, even if you already caught one: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, a new one is released at each later League win
facts.If you flee: It moves to another route with the same HP
facts.If you defeat it: It stops roaming until your next League win

entries.summary: Route 25, the cape north of Cerulean
marker: It waits here once Misty is beaten.
entries.start: Suicune does not roam. It shows itself in five places across two regions, then waits for you on Route 25.
need: The Cascade Badge from Misty.
Each sighting below, in order. They are on the story’s own path.
steps: Ecruteak City: wake the three beasts in the Burned Tower’s basement.
Cianwood City: Suicune stands on the north shore. Walk up to it. It leaves, and Eusine challenges you: see [[johto/cianwood-city|Cianwood City]].
Route 42, between Ecruteak and Mahogany: it appears once more as you cross the route.
Vermilion City, in Kanto: a sighting with Eusine as you walk through the city.
Route 14, south of Lavender: one more glimpse partway along the route.
Beat Misty in Cerulean Gym. If you beat her before the Route 14 sighting, the sighting itself completes this step.
Go to the far end of Route 25, the cape by Bill’s house. Eusine is watching. Walk up to Suicune and talk to it.
encounter: A single wild battle at Level 50. It can be caught.
after: Eusine speaks to you and leaves for Celadon City.
Having fought it here once, Suicune returns to the cape after each later League win: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, after each later League win
facts.If you defeat it: It leaves until your next League win

entries.summary: Ilex Forest shrine, with the GS Ball
entries.start: The Ho-Oh panel puzzle in the Ruins of Alph, which hides the GS Ball beneath it.
need: Kurt, in his house in Azalea Town.
The {{item:Gs Ball|GS Ball}}.
steps: In the Ruins of Alph, solve the sliding-panel puzzle that shows Ho-Oh. The floor gives way and drops you into {{map:RuinsOfAlph_B1F_hns|the basement}}, where the GS Ball now lies as an item ball.
Take it to Kurt in Azalea Town and talk to him. He takes the ball to examine it, it starts to shake, and something outside startles him.
Step outside. Kurt follows you out and hands the GS Ball back.
Go to the shrine in {{map:IlexForest_hns|Ilex Forest}} and examine it. Agree to place the GS Ball in the hole.
encounter: Celebi appears at Level 40. It can be caught.
This battle happens once per GS Ball. Whatever the result, including running away, Celebi is gone when it ends. Save before you touch the shrine.
after: Kurt meets you in the forest afterwards.
If you caught it: after each later League win a second Celebi stands in Ilex Forest at Level 40, and that one stays if you flee.
If you did not: after your next later League win the GS Ball is back in the Ruins of Alph basement and Kurt will look at it again. See {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, after each later League win
facts.If you flee: First battle: Celebi is gone. Later Celebi: it stays.
facts.If you defeat it: Gone until your next League win
facts.Can it be missed?: No, but the first chance ends with the battle

entries.start: Bill’s house at the end of Route 25. There is no wild Galarian Articuno: you convert one you already own.
need: An Articuno in your party: see {{mon:SPECIES_ARTICUNO|Articuno}}.
Bill’s Teleporter unlocked.
steps: Talk to Bill’s grandfather. He asks to see five Pokémon, one at a time: Meowth, Zigzagoon, Ponyta, Farfetch’d and Slowpoke. Bring each in your party and show it; he rewards each one.
After the fifth he tells you about Bill’s Teleporter and invites you to use the computer beside the big machine.
Use the computer, confirm, and pick Articuno from the list. It must be in your party.
encounter: No battle. The machine changes your Articuno into Galarian Articuno.
The change is permanent. The machine says so before you confirm.
after: Articuno returns to the Seafoam Islands after each later League win, so you can own both forms.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, once per Articuno you bring
facts.If you defeat it: Not a battle

entries.start: An item ball beside the truck parked on a wharf in Vermilion City’s harbour.
need: The {{item:Old Sea Map}}.
Surf, to reach the wharf.
A ship: your first crossing on the S.S. Aqua behind you. In Vermilion the sailor also wants the Machine Part returned to the Power Plant first.
steps: The truck stands on a separate wharf in Vermilion’s harbour, east of the main pier. Surf across to it and pick up the Old Sea Map beside the truck.
Talk to the sailor inside Vermilion’s port, or Olivine’s. Once the ferry is running between the regions he asks where you want to sail. Choose Faraway Island; he checks for the map.
On the island, go through to the clearing in the middle.
Mew shows itself, then hides in the tall grass and moves whenever you do. Corner it and talk to it.
encounter: A single wild battle at Level 50. It can be caught.
after: Mew is back on the island after each later League win, even if you caught it: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

entries.summary: Mt. Moon’s outdoor square, at night
marker: Touch it at night. Jirachi lands a few steps below.
entries.start: An unusual white rock on Mt. Moon’s outdoor square, the open area with the gift shop.
need: It must be night in the game. By day the rock does nothing.
steps: Go through Mt. Moon’s cave to the outdoor square.
At night, examine the white rock. “The colour reminds you of the moon. Touch it?” Say Yes.
The ground shakes and Jirachi comes down onto the square just below the rock.
Save, then talk to it.
encounter: A single wild battle at Level 50. It can be caught.
after: The rock answers once. It will call Jirachi again after each later League win: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, after each later League win
facts.If you defeat it: It leaves until your next League win

entries.when: Kanto story, or as Kanto Champion
entries.start: Steven, at Vermilion City’s north exit. He asks which you would choose: Latios or Latias.
need: If you chose Latias: nothing more. It roams.
If you chose Latios: the {{item:Eon Ticket}}, which needs the Kanto Champion title.
steps: You chose Latias. It roams Kanto at Level 60 on Routes 1 to 25. When it is on your route, each wild encounter has a one-in-four chance of being Latias. It moves as you travel and after every battle.
You chose Latios. Become Kanto Champion: see [[kanto/kanto-league|The Kanto League]].
Talk to Steven in the Safari Zone entrance building in Fuchsia City. He welcomes you to the club and gives you the Eon Ticket.
Talk to the sailor in Vermilion’s or Olivine’s port and choose Southern Island.
Walk into the island’s interior. Latias waits there at Level 50. Talk to it.
encounter: A wild battle. It can be caught.
Roaming: HP and status are kept between meetings, and a Repel keeps it away if your leading Pokémon is above Level 60.
after: After each later League win your chosen one is released again and the other is back on Southern Island: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, after each later League win
facts.If you flee: Roaming: it moves on. Island: it stays.
facts.If you defeat it: Gone until your next League win
facts.Can it be missed?: No. You get both, by different routes.

entries.when: Kanto story, or as Kanto Champion
entries.start: Steven, at Vermilion City’s north exit. He asks which you would choose: Latios or Latias.
need: If you chose Latios: nothing more. It roams.
If you chose Latias: the {{item:Eon Ticket}}, which needs the Kanto Champion title.
steps: You chose Latios. It roams Kanto at Level 60 on Routes 1 to 25. When it is on your route, each wild encounter has a one-in-four chance of being Latios. It moves as you travel and after every battle.
You chose Latias. Become Kanto Champion: see [[kanto/kanto-league|The Kanto League]].
Talk to Steven in the Safari Zone entrance building in Fuchsia City. He welcomes you to the club and gives you the Eon Ticket.
Talk to the sailor in Vermilion’s or Olivine’s port and choose Southern Island.
Walk into the island’s interior. Latios waits there at Level 50. Talk to it.
encounter: A wild battle. It can be caught.
Roaming: HP and status are kept between meetings, and a Repel keeps it away if your leading Pokémon is above Level 60.
after: After each later League win your chosen one is released again and the other is back on Southern Island: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, after each later League win
facts.If you flee: Roaming: it moves on. Island: it stays.
facts.If you defeat it: Gone until your next League win
facts.Can it be missed?: No. You get both, by different routes.

entries.start: A fan of Mary’s radio show in Olivine City, who gives the Aurora Ticket to a Kanto Champion.
need: The Kanto Champion title: see [[kanto/kanto-league|The Kanto League]].
The {{item:Aurora Ticket}}.
steps: As Kanto Champion, talk to the woman in Olivine City who jokes that her name is Mary. She recognises you from the radio and gives you the Aurora Ticket.
Talk to the sailor in Olivine’s or Vermilion’s port and choose Birth Island.
The island holds one triangular rock. Walk up to it and press A. It moves. Follow it and press A again each time.
The rock only keeps moving if you reach it in few enough steps. Too many and it returns to the start. Get it right to the end and Deoxys attacks.
encounter: A single wild battle at Level 70. It can be caught.
after: The island also has a {{item:Meteorite}} to pick up.
Deoxys and its puzzle are back after each later League win, even if you caught it: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, after each later League win
facts.If you flee: It leaves, and the puzzle is reset when you re-enter the island
facts.If you defeat it: It leaves until your next League win

entries.summary: Sinjoh Ruins temple, behind the sealed door
entries.start: The temple at the Sinjoh Ruins, which has five ancient sensors and a sealed door.
need: Regirock, Regice, Registeel, Regieleki and Regidrago, all caught: 15 plates. See {{quest:sinjoh|The seventeen plates of Sinjoh}}.
steps: Catch all five Regis from their chambers.
Enter the temple. Each sensor is looking for one of the five. Examine a sensor with the matching Regi in your party and “the temple responds to your actions.”
They do not all have to be in your party at once: each sensor remembers. Swap at a PC and come back if you need to.
At the fifth, “the way is open.” Go through the door.
Regigigas stands in the room beyond. Save, then talk to it.
encounter: A single wild battle at Level 80. It can be caught.
after: The door stays open.
Regigigas is back after each later League win: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, after each later League win
facts.If you defeat it: It leaves until your next League win
facts.Can it be missed?: No. A Regi you knocked out returns at your next League win.

entries.when: After sixteen Badges; Sinjoh, all 17 plates
entries.summary: Sinjoh Ruins, the hall above the stairway
entries.start: The end of the Sinjoh story. Arceus is fought twice in a row, and only the second battle can be won with a Poké Ball.
need: All seventeen plates, the last from Steven: see {{quest:sinjoh|The seventeen plates of Sinjoh}}.
The {{item:Azure Flute}}.
A team that can win a long battle at Level 100, with something left for a second one straight after.
steps: Beat Steven on the stairway at the Sinjoh Ruins. He gives you the Stone Plate and heals your party.
Climb into the hall and walk forward. “The Azure Flute is reacting. Play the flute?” Say Yes. ||Light gathers and Arceus appears in the hall.||
Save now. Then talk to Arceus.

First battle. ||Arceus is Level 100 and Steel-type, holding the Iron Plate, with Judgment, Hydro Pump, Recover and Dazzling Gleam. It starts with Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def and accuracy each raised two stages.|| You cannot throw a Ball and you cannot run. Knock it out.

Second battle. It follows at once, with no chance to heal in between. ||Arceus is now Level 80 and Normal-type, with Extreme Speed, Earth Power, Recover and Hyper Beam, and no boosts.|| The game asks whether it can be caught: it can. Catch it.
encounter: Two wild battles, back to back. Only the second can end in a capture.
If you run from the second battle, Arceus stays in the hall. Talk to it again and you go straight to the second battle: the first is never repeated.
after: On your way out Steven congratulates you. Let that scene play: it is what allows Arceus to return.
If you knocked Arceus out in the second battle, it is back in the hall after your next later League win: {{quest:league-reset|How legendaries return}}.
The seventeen plates are held items. The game defines an Arceus form for each plate’s type.

facts.Repeatable: Yes, the Level 80 battle, after each later League win
facts.If you flee: First battle: not allowed. Second: it stays.
facts.If you defeat it: First battle: required. Second: it leaves until your next League win

entries.start: The Sky Pillar on Route 131. During the story Rayquaza only wakes and leaves; it is there to be caught after the credits.
need: The Hoenn League won: see [[hoenn/hoenn-league|The Hoenn League]].
Surf, and the Bicycle for the Sky Pillar’s cracked floors.
steps: After the credits, return to the Sky Pillar.
Climb it. The floors are cracked now: ride the Bicycle in straight lines across cracked tiles. Stop on one, or cross on foot, and you fall to the floor below.
Rayquaza is at the top. Save, then talk to it.
encounter: A single wild battle at Level 85. It can be caught.
after: One per save. Once the Pokédex shows Rayquaza as caught, it is never offered again.
If you knock it out, it is back after your next Hoenn League win. This is Hoenn’s League, not Kanto’s.

facts.Repeatable: No. One catch per save.
facts.If you flee: It flies off; it is back when you return to the summit
facts.If you defeat it: It is back after your next Hoenn League win

entries.start: The north of Route 127, where it rains after the League. The researcher upstairs in the Weather Institute on Route 119 will tell you where to look.
need: The Hoenn League won: see [[hoenn/hoenn-league|The Hoenn League]].
Surf and Dive.
steps: After the credits both sites are open at once. If you want the pointer, the researcher on the Weather Institute’s upper floor names Route 127 for heavy rain or Route 114 for drought; with both legends still at large he picks one of the two at random each time you ask.
Surf to the north of Route 127. It is raining there. The map below marks the place to Dive.
Dive, enter the Marine Cave and go through to its end.
Kyogre waits in the water. Save, then approach it.
encounter: A single wild battle at Level 85. It can be caught.
after: When Kyogre is caught or defeated, the rain on Route 127 stops and the cave closes.
One per save. Once the Pokédex shows Kyogre as caught, it is never offered again.
If you knock it out, the cave reopens after your next Hoenn League win.

facts.Repeatable: No. One catch per save.
facts.If you flee: It leaves; it is back when you return to the cave’s end
facts.If you defeat it: It is back after your next Hoenn League win

absent.lead: The engine Project Blonde is built on defines many more Legendary and Mythical Pokémon than the game uses. These have no encounter, gift, trade, egg or evolution in this build, so they have no guide and no Pokédex page. No Trainer uses one either.
notes: Lillie’s story on the Alola isles is Project Blonde’s own and does not involve Cosmog.
The Red Orb and Blue Orb appear in Hoenn’s story but no script gives either to you, so the Primal forms are not available.
The sealed chambers are not part of this game’s Hoenn. Regirock, Regice and Registeel are in Sinjoh instead.
Not in the game. Ho-Oh and Lugia are in Johto.
